PullRequest.Title: chat: Add Copilot connectors as an authenticated customization source
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Adds an independently gated, authenticated Copilot Connectors source to the customization Marketplace and MCP management UI.

- Keeps connector discovery and consent separate from the anonymous GitHub Feed and MCP Gallery. Desktop requests use a scoped native channel with typed operations, bounded responses, cancellation, and per-request credentials; web uses the workbench request path.
- Preserves normal default-account sign-in scopes. Generic catalog browsing uses an ordinary GitHub session when supported. **Check Connection** and connection actions explicitly request missing connector permission for the same account; rollout-time HTTP 403 responses remain recoverable and never trigger passive consent.
- Composes connector results with other Marketplace sources using bounded ranked search and round-robin browse. One source failing, requiring sign-in, or being disabled does not hide healthy sources.
- Shows connected connector MCP servers under **Installed** and products under **Connectors**, with status-aware actions, details, explicit empty states, and user/workspace MCP precedence.
- Gates connector discovery and Copilot session availability on the default-off `chat.customizations.copilotConnectors.enabled` setting. Marketplace visibility remains independently controlled by `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled`.
- Scopes session-time support to the Copilot Agent Host provider. VS Code retains the pre-session catalog and consent UI, while the bundled Copilot runtime owns session-time connector reconciliation, validation, managed MCP projection, credentials, collision handling, and lifecycle through `session.rpc.connectors.*`.
- Awaits runtime reconciliation before a Copilot session becomes available, so a connector that was just connected is usable in the first fresh session. Reconciliation failure is non-fatal to ordinary Copilot chat.

VS Code does not project connector endpoints or forward GitHub credentials to them. Credential delivery remains runtime-owned and endpoint-bound.

## Validation

- 1,064 changed-file unit tests pass locally (1 existing pending).
- `npm run typecheck-client` passes.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` passes.
- Changed-file ESLint passes.
- Copilot Agent Host runtime-MCP lifecycle replay passes.
- Twelve connector/MCP component fixtures render without errors and remain stable in dark and light themes, including the empty Connectors tab and connector detail.
- Live verification connected Microsoft Learn Docs, created a completely fresh Copilot Agent session, invoked the runtime-managed `microsoft_docs_search` tool, and returned an official Microsoft Learn result. The connector was disconnected after validation.

## Manual test

1. Toggle Marketplace visibility separately from the public GitHub Feed and Copilot Connectors settings. With Marketplace off, verify Overview and legacy MCP management remain available. With Marketplace on, verify Discover and each enabled source independently.
2. Search, browse, filter, paginate, and fail or disable each source independently. Healthy results must remain available and retry must restart from the first page.
3. Start signed out, sign in with ordinary GitHub scopes, and browse the generic connector catalog without a connector-consent prompt when the backend permits it. Use **Check Connection** or **Connect** to explicitly upgrade the same account. Verify cancellation and recoverable rollout-time HTTP 403 behavior.
4. Connect and disconnect a connector. Verify its status and details, its connected MCP servers under **Installed**, and user/workspace MCP precedence.
5. Create a fresh Copilot Agent session immediately after connecting and invoke one of the connector's MCP tools. Disable the connector experiment and verify fresh Copilot sessions no longer expose connector tools.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The duplicate call is explicit on the loaded critical path, and both render branches perform full synchronous collection/DOM work. Exact milliseconds depend on accumulated results and host performance, but the doubled mechanism and navigation trigger are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work, allocations, DOM nodes, list updates, and layout work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The duplicated synchronous work grows with the number of loaded search results and recorded resources; in browse mode it recreates every displayed section/card and associated listeners and image elements.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased navigation latency, CPU/GC pressure, and potential UI jank when reopening Discover
Findings.PreviousBehavior: When setVisible(true) found an already-loaded catalog, the existing else branch called render() once before scheduling layout.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added unconditional render() runs immediately after that existing else-branch render, so the cached/loaded path now performs the complete render twice for one visibility transition.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1783 adds an unconditional this.render() after the unchanged else branch already calls this.render() for loaded pages.
Findings.Title: Avoid rendering the loaded Discover page twice
Findings.Impact: Returning to an already-loaded Discover page (including after scrolling through multiple result pages) synchronously rebuilds the list or card DOM twice before the next frame, delaying the section switch and doubling transient allocations/layout work.
Findings.Evidence: setVisible(true) enters the else branch whenever no initial/recovery catalog load is needed, calls render() there, then reaches the newly added render() at line 1783. renderSearchResults iterates catalog and recorded resources and replaces the full WorkbenchList via splice; renderBrowse clears browseSections and browseDisposables and recreates all sections, cards, listeners, and image elements, and render() invokes layout.
Findings.Recommendation: Render once per visibility transition: keep the existing else-branch render for loaded state, and only perform the new immediate render in the catalog-loading branch (or remove the unconditional call if loadCatalog already establishes the loading UI).

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or return to Discover, browse the composed marketplace, and search connector metadata
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A visibility transition synchronously renders the cached page; a cold/expired query additionally resolves the default authentication session, crosses desktop IPC, fetches the connector catalog, validates/parses it, ranks search results locally, merges sources, and renders the list. Warm search ranking and pagination use cached snapshots and avoid the network.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the bounded connector operation and per-request credential to the shared process on desktop
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC call for a cold/expired connector catalog refresh; zero for warm searches and continuation pages
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The connector source and its dedicated IPC channel did not exist
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks cold catalog availability before results can render

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET /plugins and read/parse a response capped at 5 MiB
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for a cold/expired refresh; the 60-second service cache and pinned continuations make warm searches and pagination local
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No connector catalog request was made
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks cold connector discovery; other marketplace sources continue independently

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve silent authentication-provider sessions for the active default account
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider-session lookup per catalog refresh, including polling refreshes; zero on warm getConnectors cache hits
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Connector discovery did not resolve this scoped session

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to 1,000 connectors, up to 16 search words, bounded metadata arrays and strings, and the number of search pages accumulated in the UI. The reported duplicate render scales with loaded catalog plus recorded resources.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Marketplace sources are queried concurrently by the aggregator. Within the connector source one query performs one catalog refresh, but cold refresh promises are not globally coalesced. Connector continuations are sequential cursor reads over a pinned snapshot; the source LRU is capped at 32.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The catalog is fresh for 60 seconds. Search snapshots pin up to 1,000 parsed connectors for 30 minutes in a 32-entry LRU, and account/session/enablement changes cancel their cache token. Continuation pages reuse the snapshot without network work; negative/no-account results do not set a fresh timestamp.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the network/cache path and the duplicate synchronous render are explicit; the added line deterministically executes after the existing loaded-state render.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact UI delay depends on loaded-result count, DOM/list implementation, and machine speed; this affects severity, not the proven duplicate work.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated synchronous rendering: reopening an already-loaded Discover page now rebuilds its list or card DOM twice. Catalog transport, response allocation, local search, and continuation retention are bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect, reconnect, check, or disconnect a Copilot connector from Discover or connector details
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An explicit action resolves/creates the scoped authentication session, sends PUT or DELETE, optionally opens browser consent, then polls the authoritative catalog until the status changes. Completion waits for the catalog result; a membership change also awaits the throttled Agent Host refresh bridge.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Silent authentication session lookup and, after explicit consent, authentication-session creation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one lookup per operation; session creation occurs only when scoped permission is absent and is coalesced across simultaneous authorization attempts
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks connection mutation until the correct account credential is available

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: PUT or DELETE connector membership, followed by GET /plugins status polling
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mutation plus one immediate refresh and then one GET every two seconds until success, bounded by five minutes (up to about 150 polling refreshes)
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No connector membership mutation or status polling existed
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The user action remains pending until an authoritative status is observed or timeout/cancellation occurs

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Notify the local Agent Host to mark live Copilot sessions stale after connected membership changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One throttled management call for a detected membership change; unchanged polls do not trigger it
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the refresh that observes the change so the next live-session turn uses new membership

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Time spent completing browser consent controls poll count; concurrent distinct connector actions control aggregate request rate.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Authorization creation is coalesced by authorizationPromise and Agent Host refreshes by a Throttler. The install service deduplicates an operation for the same connector key, while distinct connector actions can proceed concurrently. Each operation polls serially every two seconds for at most five minutes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Action polling intentionally bypasses the 60-second getConnectors freshness check by calling refresh directly. Unchanged parsed catalogs are deep-equality suppressed, while membership changes invalidate live sessions. Cancellation, experiment disablement, account changes, and disposal stop the operation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: intervals, timeout, serial polling, per-action deduplication, and throttled Agent Host refresh are explicit and tested.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical consent duration and frequency of users starting multiple connector actions are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. Polling can issue many bounded requests but is cancellation-aware, serial per operation, and necessary to await an authoritative asynchronous status; evidence is insufficient that its two-second cadence is a concrete user performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create, resume, or refresh a Copilot agent session while connectors are enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing Copilot client/session launch remains on the chat startup or next-turn path. After session creation/resume and safety/sandbox setup, launch now awaits connector capabilities, session GitHub auth status, client account enumeration, and runtime reconciliation before exposing the session. A live membership change queues stale marks behind active turns; the next turn destroys/resumes each affected session and performs reconciliation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start or restart the Copilot runtime client with account token authentication when connector credentials change
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing client startup is reused; at most one deferred restart is requested for the observed connector-authentication mismatch
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: GitHub.com sessions without enterprise authentication did not require a client restart for connector-scoped credential changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A session launch waits until the correctly authenticated client is available

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call runtime RPCs for connector capabilities, GitHub auth status, account enumeration, and connector reconciliation with catalog refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four sequential RPC calls for each created or resumed session when enabled and capabilities are available; zero when the feature is disabled and reconciliation stops early after capabilities when unavailable
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Session launch performed none of these connector RPCs
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Explicitly blocks session availability so a newly connected tool is present on the first turn

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queue a stale marker for every live Copilot backing after membership changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One in-memory queued operation per live session/chat, deduplicated at the upstream membership-change notification level
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Membership changes did not fan out to live sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the current active-turn critical path; the next turn pays one session refresh/reconciliation

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of newly created/resumed sessions and number of live sessions when membership changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The four runtime RPC stages are sequential for each launched session. Live-session stale marking fans out with Promise.all across sessions but each mark is queued behind that chat's sequencer. Client restarts are coalesced/deferred around active turns.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The client authentication tuple is retained and compared before session launch. Runtime reconciliation intentionally requests a fresh catalog for every created/resumed session; no result cache is maintained in VS Code. Unchanged connector catalogs do not trigger live-session invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: startup placement, sequential RPC order, fan-out, and queueing behind active turns are direct in the diff and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime RPC and remote catalog durations, plus typical live-session counts, are not measured in the repository.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The new RPC latency is an explicit connector feature contract—reconciliation must complete before session availability—and failure is non-fatal; no safe narrower call or redundant invocation was established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Installed MCP view and display connected connector MCP servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the MCP section becomes visible with access enabled, existing MCP refresh proceeds and connector discovery calls getConnectors. A warm catalog returns immediately; a cold catalog uses the authenticated IPC/network path. Filtering then merges connected connector servers with local, built-in, plugin, extension, and active-session entries and updates the tree.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh connector catalog when no fresh catalog is available
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on a service-cache hit within 60 seconds; otherwise one authentication lookup, desktop IPC call, and GET /plugins
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The MCP view did not fetch connector state
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Does not block initial widget construction; results update the installed tree asynchronously

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build connector MCP entries and merge them into installed entries
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pass over connected connector MCP servers per refresh/change/filter event, bounded by 1,000 connectors and 64 servers each by response validation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No connector MCP rows were merged
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous tree-filter/update work while the section is visible

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Count of connected connectors and their validated MCP servers, plus existing installed/runtime MCP entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing MCP refresh and connector refresh are started independently. Only one current widget connector request token is retained; a newer refresh cancels the prior one. Connector action requests have a separate cancellation owner.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses the shared 60-second connector catalog cache. Connector change listeners are installed only while the experiment is enabled, hidden/access-disabled states cancel requests, and unchanged service state suppresses events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: visibility gates, cancellation, cache use, and merge loops are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Real connected-server counts are likely far below validation maxima.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The cold boundary is asynchronous and cached, and synchronous merge work is linear in the actual connected server count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Persist and reconcile account-scoped connector installation records
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On an authoritative connector change, the install service scans connected connectors, derives account-scoped records, hashes IDs only for new records, upserts changed metadata into profile storage, then reconciles applicable connector records against the in-memory catalog.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize identity and compute SHA-256 for a new account-scoped record ID
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per connected connector lacking an existing record; existing records reuse their ID
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No connector records or connector identity hashes existed
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off catalog rendering's direct critical path, invoked asynchronously from the change listener

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist new or metadata-changed connector installation records in profile storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one upsert per connected connector whose record is absent or changed for the active account
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No connector record storage writes occurred
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous bookkeeping after connector state changes

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of connected connectors and number of changed/missing records for the active account.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The change listener invokes one asynchronous synchronization per emitted service change; identical catalog refreshes are equality-suppressed. Record reconciliation uses the service's existing bounded reconciliation flow.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The parsed connector catalog is authoritative in memory; deep-equal refreshes emit no change. Existing record IDs are reused, and only changed metadata is upserted. Account and experiment gates limit applicable records.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for loop and write conditions; exact storage implementation cost is less certain.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical connected connector count and profile-storage latency are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Work is change-driven, skips unchanged record writes, and scales with connected rather than all available connectors.

Scenarios.Scenario: Authenticate the Agent Host against GitHub while connector preference is enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing protected-resource resolver first obtains a usable GitHub session. For api.github.com only, the change performs one additional silent lookup for sessions on the same account and selects the narrowest already-authorized connector-scoped superset before forwarding a token.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Silently enumerate authentication sessions for the resolved provider/account
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extra provider-session lookup for each applicable GitHub protected-resource resolution when enabled and the initially resolved session lacks connector scope; zero otherwise
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The initially resolved usable GitHub session was forwarded without this second lookup
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks forwarding the selected token to the Agent Host for that authentication pass

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of applicable GitHub protected-resource authentication passes, normally one resource per Agent Host reconciliation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Protected resources are processed sequentially by the existing loop. The added lookup is one awaited provider query per applicable resolution; it does not prompt or create sessions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing auth token cache avoids forwarding unchanged tokens, but the additional session enumeration itself is not cached here. Authentication-session change events drive later reconciliation elsewhere.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: condition, lookup, and cardinality are explicit and covered by tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider lookup latency and authentication reconciliation frequency are not established as hot.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. This is one gated silent lookup on an infrequent authentication path, with no realistic scaling trigger shown.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 56 changed files and relevant call paths. Submitted one medium repeated-render finding. Connector discovery uses bounded responses, a 60-second catalog cache, account-invalidated snapshots, and 32-entry continuation LRU; explicit connector actions use bounded cancellable polling; Agent Host reconciliation adds intentional sequential runtime RPCs before enabled sessions become available and queues live-session refreshes behind turns.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
